rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) an email found in a breach corpus — exposure alone is not misconduct; corroborate with Hashcrack before denying.
Deny any candidate whose claimed GitHub does not match their commit email history.
Deny any candidate who behaves hostilely or threatens the service.
Deny any candidate whose submitted logs show brute-force activity from their account.
Deny any candidate who submits an image with a covert embedded payload.
Deny any candidate whose logs show a credential-stuffing sweep (one source hitting many accounts).
Deny any candidate whose logs reveal a low-and-slow intrusion spread to evade detection.
Deny any candidate who submits an image hiding an encrypted/obfuscated payload.
Deny any candidate whose submitted credential cracks to a password found in a known breach corpus.
Deny any candidate still submitting a credential whose plaintext recurs across multiple breach corpora.
Deny any candidate submitting an unsalted / plaintext-equivalent credential — it cracks on the first attempt.
Deny any candidate whose handle matches a known threat / dark-web forum account.
Deny any candidate whose submitted credential is unsalted / plaintext-equivalent — the password is exposed outright on the dossier.
Flag (do not auto-deny) a claimed connection IP that does not match the submitted logs — corroborate before denying.
Flag (do not auto-deny) a weakly-encrypted credential that cracks to a weak password — poor hygiene, not proof of malice.
Flag (do not auto-deny) a password stored with weak encryption (MD5) — a hygiene issue, not proof the password itself is weak.
Flag (do not auto-deny) a handle with almost no public presence — corroborate before denying.
Flag (do not auto-deny) a dossier with no affiliation stated — an omission, not proof of anything.
Deny any candidate whose handle appears across a network of sock-puppet accounts.
Deny any candidate whose dossier affiliation does not match the organisation on their public profiles.
Flag (do not auto-deny) a candidate whose public profiles list no organisation at all.
Deny any candidate whose email domain is a known disposable / throwaway service.
Deny any candidate whose logins occur from locations too far apart to be travelled between.
Deny any candidate whose logs show after-hours access combined with privilege escalation.
Deny any candidate whose submitted image hides a covert command-and-control beacon.
Deny any candidate whose public accounts were all created within days of each other.
Flag (do not auto-deny) a handle that is a lookalike of a listed organisation's handle.
Flag (do not auto-deny) activity outside business hours — common enough to be innocent alone.
Deny any candidate whose cracked password recurs across multiple breach corpora.

rule_sheet.summary: Dossier only today. Deny a throwaway email address, a stored password you can read, or anyone who threatens the service. Everything else is an admit.

affiliations: "independent" / "freelance" — thin, but not disqualifying on its own

notes: A blank affiliation is an omission, not a lie — flag it, don't deny on it.
MD5 on the strength chip is poor hygiene, not proof of anything. Flag.
UNSALTED is different: the password is printed in the clear. That is a deny.
